David Heinemeier Hansson thinks the agent era is reopening a window in computing that has been closed for decades: the chance to build a new operating system people actually want to use.

DHH joins a16z General Partners Martin Casado and Anish Acharya to explain why he’s building Omarchy, an agent-first Linux distribution designed around a computer that users can modify simply by asking.

They discuss why the command lines, config files, and detailed error messages that once made Linux intimidating now make it unusually well suited to agents, and why DHH believes software development has become cheap enough to challenge decades-old platform lock-in.

videos.title: Why Nick Bostrom Thinks Superintelligence Could End Aging
videos.description:
The question isn’t simply whether humanity should race toward superintelligence or stop. Nick Bostrom argues the harder challenge is preserving the ability to slow down when safety falls behind, without turning a temporary pause into permanent technological stagnation.

a16z’s Eddy Lazzarin and Elena Burger sit down with Bostrom to revisit the ideas he helped bring into the mainstream, now that increasingly capable AI systems actually exist. NVIDIA announced CUDA in 2006 as a different way to compute - giving developers direct access to the parallel power of the GPU.

Two decades later, the CUDA platform is enabling work in scientific computing, professional visualization, autonomous vehicles, drug discovery and healthcare, generative AI, robotics and more.

Today, more than 11 million developers are leveraging CUDA for their work and a new generation of students, researchers and builders continue to shape the future. We’re celebrating 20 years of CUDA and honoring the architects of progress.

videos.title: 'We Have To Know Why': Philanthropist Priscilla Chan’s Bold Bet On Rare Disease
videos.description:
In just a decade, rare disease groups have gone from not understanding certain genetic mutations to bringing gene therapies into clinical trials. Priscilla Chan joins Becky Quick to discuss rare disease research, personalized medicine and how AI could help advance biomedicine and science.

Chan and her husband, Mark Zuckerberg, the founder of Meta, co-founded the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI) and Biohub, both with a core mission of curing, preventing, or managing all disease. Drawing on her background as a pediatrician, Chan explains how rare disease groups are building research programs, patient registries and clinical trials, and how this work could point to new approaches for treating diseases more broadly.
